A1.justification: Both PDFs describe QHFlow2 and retain corresponding methods, benchmarks, and results. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Hamiltonian, energy, and force evaluations, scaling experiments, ablations, SCF convergence tests, and bond-stretching analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds benchmark evaluations, force-consistency tests, geometry optimization, and further analyses in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The proposed SO(2) backbone, two-stage pair update, residual flow-matching formulation, priors, and training/sampling algorithms remain unchanged. The density-only and joint-output variants in G.11 are experimental alternatives; they do not replace the default Hamiltonian-prediction method.

E1.justification: v2 adds training and evaluation on drug-like molecules in ∇2DFT and zero-shot evaluation on PubChemQH molecules with 45–98 atoms. Geometry optimization and local potential-energy-surface evaluation also extend the task coverage beyond the retained snapshot-prediction benchmarks.

E2.justification: v2 adds QHNetV2 to the QH9 comparisons in Table 2, trained eSEN baselines on rMD17 in Table 19, and xTB/MMFF comparators for geometry optimization in Table 25. HELM, SchNOrb, and PhiSNet were already compared in v1 Table 12; their appearance on ∇2DFT is an extension of coverage.

E3.justification: The reported SCF tolerance changes from 10^-13 in v1 E.4 to 10^-9 in v2 G.3. New protocols include a 1,920-GPU-hour ∇2DFT training cap, finite-difference force checks on 10 geometries per molecule, and BFGS optimization and Hessian evaluations with specified stopping thresholds and displacement steps.

E4.justification: v2 adds readout-degree and prediction-target ablations, large-molecule extrapolation, empirical error-scaling fits, analytic-versus-finite-difference force checks, orbital-subspace error decomposition, and geometry/PES diagnostics. These investigate substantial new questions. The original bond-stretching analysis is retained as G.10, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v2 introduces numerical ± summaries in Tables 23, 26, and 27 and fitted exponents with R² values in Table 22. The meaning of the ± quantities is not specified, and no increased training-run or seed count is established. The existing statement about fixing random seeds remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Most existing MD/QH9 scores remain unchanged, but v2 adds extensive results, including ∇2DFT accuracy, large-molecule failures, force-consistency measurements, and local PES errors. Figure 4 also changes: QHFlow2-l's SCF cycle ratio moves from 52.8% to 47.4%. Because the reported convergence tolerance changes, this is not a demonstrated same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: G.8 adds a perturbative derivation of second-order energy error versus first-order force error, with particle-number conservation and nondegenerate/gapped-orbital conditions. It also formalizes integrated density error and molecular-orbital block decomposition. These additions go beyond v1's retained DFT and equivariance background.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions and headline claims: the QHFlow2 architecture, direct energy/force benchmarking, improved Hamiltonian accuracy, NequIP-level force accuracy, and favorable scaling. New supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explains the energy–force error gap and why global Hamiltonian MAE can misrepresent downstream accuracy. It interprets large-molecule failures through orbital ill-conditioning and explicitly acknowledges that one-shot forces need not be conservative. These substantially refine the mechanism discussion and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 adds implementation disclosures about the single-Fock-build evaluation, B3LYP(VWN5) convention, SCF post-processing and H200 hardware, and two-H200/DDP training for ∇2DFT. The core architecture/training tables, software disclosures, and code-access information remain largely unchanged.

R1.justification: The new discussion in Section 3.3 and Appendix D.3 substantially expands positioning against HELM and QHNetV2, distinguishing their backbones, Hamiltonian readouts, pair refinement, and downstream energy evaluation. QHNetV2 is newly cited, while several ancillary reactivity references are removed.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 rewrites the conclusion and bond-stretching discussion, adds explanatory cross-references, moves SCF documentation from E.4 to G.3, and updates publication and acknowledgement text. The extensive new scientific material does not constitute a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds twelve tables displaying new evaluations and analyses and expands Table 2 with QHNetV2 rows. Figure 4 is relocated and resized, Figure 6's reversed left/right caption is corrected, and the retained Figure 8 is integrated into a different appendix layout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation beyond v1's snapshot accuracy and scaling results. Force-consistency and local PES tests in Tables 23–27 address practical-use questions, while Table 21 and the conservative-force caveat make important failure boundaries explicit. The added comparisons and chemical coverage further strengthen the evidence. Some new documentation needs correction: Equation 27 does not reconcile its exchange-correlation potential expression with the energy definitions in Equations 23–25, and the ± summaries are undefined. These weaknesses do not outweigh the substantial gains in validation and qualification of the central claims.
